name: Esau
charge: Despising his birthright; marrying the daughters of Heth against the fathers’ law; purposing to kill his brother
summary: The first came out red, all over like a hairy garment, and his birth had to be documented because a nation comes out of him; from him comes Edom, which is red, and this teaching reads his seed as the return of Cain’s line. He was the firstborn as Cain was the firstborn, a man of the field as Cain was, and carnal minded: he sold the birthright for a meal, took Hittite wives to his parents’ grief, and when the blessing went to Jacob he purposed in his heart to kill him. His own anger turned away; his children’s never did.
offenseFull: The first came out red, all over like a hairy garment, and they called his name Esau; Jacob is not described, because he looked like his father and his mother and like everybody from the time of Adam (Genesis 25:25-26). The scribes wrote down the colour of the one who was different, because a nation comes out of him. Esau means wasted away, and what was wasted away was the pigment; the hair over him covers a body with no protection of its own from the sun, and it is thin and goatlike, which is why goat skins passed for it. Jacob’s hand took hold on Esau’s heel, and that is prophecy: Esau is the end of this world, and Jacob the beginning of it that follows (2 Esdras 6:7-9). He was a cunning hunter, a man of the field, as Cain was a man of the field; Cain was the firstborn and Esau was the firstborn, and it is the same spirit (Genesis 25:27; Genesis 4:2).

He came from the field faint and asked to be fed with that same red pottage, which had red meat in it, and that is why his name was called Edom, red; he asked what profit the birthright should do him, sware, sold it for bread and pottage of lentiles, rose up and went his way (Genesis 25:29-34). He wanted the carnal thing and threw away the thing from above; it was not taken from him. Hebrews names him a profane person and a fornicator, and the fornication is in the law he broke: at forty he took to wife Judith and Bashemath, daughters of the Hittites, which were a grief of mind to Isaac and to Rebekah, and later he went to Ishmael and took Mahalath also (Hebrews 12:16; Genesis 26:34-35; Genesis 28:8-9; Tobit 4:12). That is the nature of the vessel, and Hebrews names the root: a root of bitterness springing up, and thereby many defiled (Hebrews 12:15).

When the blessing went to Jacob he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry and wept aloud, which is worldly sorrow; he told his father that Jacob had supplanted him these two times, playing the victim over a birthright he sold (Genesis 27:34-38; Psalms 50:19-20). He found no place of repentance, though he sought it with tears (Hebrews 12:17). He hated Jacob because of the blessing, and said in his heart that the days of mourning for his father were at hand and then he would slay his brother (Genesis 27:41). Cain killed Abel; Esau purposed to kill Jacob. Rebekah knew that if he did it she would be deprived of both in one day, because the man who kills his brother dies for it (Genesis 27:45; Wisdom of Solomon 10:3).
judgmentFull: His portion was given him: his dwelling should be the fatness of the earth and of the dew of heaven from above, and by his sword he should live, and he should serve his brother; and when he should have the dominion he should break his brother’s yoke from off his neck (Genesis 27:39-40). What his kingdoms have, they took by war and by ever more advanced weaponry, the same inheritance Cain’s line carried through Tubalcain (Genesis 4:22). He broke the yoke in the days of Jehoram, when Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah and made a king over themselves (2 Kings 8:20); this present time is the time of his dominion, and when his rule is done, Jacob comes into power.

His own anger turned away; his children’s did not, and the perpetual hatred remained in his seed (Ezekiel 35:5). In the day that the strangers carried Judah away he stood as one of them, rejoiced over their destruction, laid hands on their substance and cut off those that escaped, and the Edomites burned the temple (Obadiah

1:11-14; 1 Esdras 4:45). The Lord said he loved Jacob and hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste; though Edom says they will return and build the desolate places, they shall build and he will throw down, and they shall be called the border of wickedness, the people against whom the Lord has indignation for ever (Malachi 1:2-4). For his violence against his brother Jacob shame shall cover him, and the house of Esau shall be stubble, with none remaining (Obadiah 1:10, 18). Though he exalt himself as the eagle and set his nest among the stars, from there he shall be brought down (Obadiah 1:3-4). The descendants of Esau, sworn enemies of the descendants of Jacob even to the end of the world, went out from Mount Seir and founded Rome and its empire, and hold dominion over Europe, Esau detaining his brother Jacob in captivity; those prophecies have not yet received their full accomplishment.

lawsResolved.text: Birthright of the firstborn can be sold to another son .
Birthright of firstborn son can be lost and given up to another son if the firstborn commits a sin against the family.
We are not to intermarry with those who practice idolatry.

text.text: And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.
And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau’s heel; and his name was called Jacob: and Isaac was threescore years old when she bare them.
And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.
Then answered I and said, What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?
And he said unto me, From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.
For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.
And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint:
And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.
And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.
And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?
And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob.
Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.
Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.
For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.
And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:
Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.
And Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father;
Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.

Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe: for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.
Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled;
And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father.
And he said, Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing.

And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?

And Isaac answered and said unto Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and with corn and wine have I sustained him: and what shall I do now unto thee, my son?
And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.
And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above;
And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.
Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit.
Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.
And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.
Until thy brother’s anger turn away from thee, and he forget that which thou hast done to him: then I will send, and fetch thee from thence: why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?
But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.
And Zillah, she also bare Tubal–cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal–cain was Naamah.
In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.
Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end:

In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them.

But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; neither shouldest thou have spoken proudly in the day of distress.

Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity; yea, thou shouldest not have looked on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance in the day of their calamity;
Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape; neither shouldest thou have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.
Thou also hast vowed to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.
I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob,
And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.

Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.
For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.

And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.
The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?
Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.
And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
